source.title_on_document: How and for Whom Using Generative AI Affects Creativity: A Field Experiment

supplement.where: https://doi.org/10.1037/apl0001296.supp (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1, below keywords)
supplement.holds: Multilevel results without control variables (text cites Supplemental Table S5 Model 4 for usefulness without controls: 0.28, SE 0.11, p = .009; footnote 2 cites Supplemental Materials S4 for the no-controls models), item-level analyses of cognitive job resources (Supplemental Tables S1-S4), and robustness tests on the moderator and practical significance of moderated mediation (Supplemental Sections S6-S8).

paper_design_summary: In a technology consulting firm in China, 250 nonmanagerial employees were randomly assigned on August 7, 2023 to receive ChatGPT accounts (with usage examples) or no LLM access. On August 15, 2023, direct supervisors rated each employee's creative performance over the week, and two external raters scored the novelty and usefulness of each employee's written response to a question on protecting employee privacy in the digital workplace. The paper also tests self-reported cognitive job resources as a mediator and self-reported metacognitive strategies as a moderator.

studies.label: Field experiment, ChatGPT access vs no access, technology consulting firm (China)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Personal ChatGPT account (via the firm's API-based interface) with usage examples, versus no LLM assistance
assignment.quote: on August 7, 2023, participants were randomly assigned to either the treatment or control group using a random number generator.
assignment.locator: PDF pp. 5-6 (printed pp. 4-5), Method, Participants and Procedure
assignment.prereg_locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 4), Transparency and Openness: "This study is not preregistered."

arms.name: LLM assistance
arms.description: Received ChatGPT accounts with usage examples, for personal use only; told ChatGPT was intended to assist, not replace, their roles. Usage logs: M = 33.72 uses (SD = 8.17); all reported use.

arms.name: Control (no LLM assistance)
arms.description: No ChatGPT account; none reported any usage (M frequency = 1, SD = 0).

participants.exclusions: 286 eligible nonmanagerial employees were invited; 36 did not participate due to business travel and illnesses before assignment, leaving 250, who were then randomly assigned. No exclusions after assignment are reported; Tables 1 and 3 report N = 250. Per-arm counts are not printed.
participants.who: Nonmanagerial employees of a technology consulting firm across technology, sales/consulting, and administration departments (excluding those already experimenting with the ChatGPT API service); 64.8% male, mean age 29.59 (SD 4.37); nested within 30 supervisors in three departments
participants.quote: Due to business travel and illnesses, 36 employees did not participate, resulting in a final sample of 250 employees.
participants.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 4), Participants and Procedure; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Results; PDF p. 7, Table 1 note (N = 250)

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT, accessed through the firm's OpenAI API-based interface (model version not stated)
ai_tool.how_used: Free use of a personal ChatGPT account in ordinary work for about one week (August 7 to August 15, 2023), with usage examples provided.

task.description: Ordinary consulting-firm work over one week (rated by supervisors for general creative performance), plus one idea-generation prompt in the second survey: suggestions for protecting employee privacy when companies use digital devices, at least 70 Chinese characters.
task.duration: About one week (assignment August 7, 2023; second survey and ratings August 15, 2023)

outcomes.name: Creativity (supervisor rating)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Direct supervisors rated each employee's general creative performance over the week on Zhou and George's (2001) creativity scale (1-5, alpha = .97), e.g. "This employee came up with creative solutions to problems." Supervisors were approached only at the end, unaware of the experiment and blind to hypotheses. The rating is of the employee's work behavior over the week, not of a specific produced output.

contrasts.reported: Table 2: control M 3.05 (SD 1.09) vs LLM assistance M 4.14 (SD 0.58); p value of t-test .000; Cohen's d 1.25 (per-arm n not printed). Table 3 Model 2 (multilevel, with controls, N = 250): gamma = 0.84, SE = 0.10, p < .001.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 7), Table 2; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 3 Model 2; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Results

outcomes.name: Novelty (external raters' rating) of privacy-protection response
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two external raters, blind to hypotheses and design, independently rated the novelty of each employee's written response (1 = least, 5 = most) following the consensual assessment technique; ICC novelty = .78. The raters' expertise is not described. The paper does not state whether treated employees could or did use ChatGPT while writing this response; their accounts were not reported as withdrawn.

contrasts.reported: Table 2: control M 2.78 (SD 0.96) vs LLM assistance M 3.11 (SD 0.95); p value of t-test .006; Cohen's d 0.35 (per-arm n not printed). Table 3 Model 3 (multilevel, with controls): gamma = 0.25, SE = 0.13, p = .049.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 7), Table 2; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 3 Model 3; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Results

outcomes.name: Usefulness (external raters' rating) of privacy-protection response
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same two external raters and response as S1-O2, usefulness rated 1-5; ICC usefulness = .69. Effect not significant with controls (Table 3) but significant without controls (Supplemental Table S5, not in this PDF).

contrasts.reported: Table 2: control M 2.87 (SD 0.82) vs LLM assistance M 3.15 (SD 0.89); p value of t-test .010; Cohen's d 0.33 (per-arm n not printed). Table 3 Model 4 (with controls): gamma = 0.17, SE = 0.11, p = .136. Without controls (Supplemental Table S5 Model 4, cited in text): gamma = 0.28, SE = 0.11, p = .009.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 7), Table 2; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 3 Model 4; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Results

company_involvement.description: No AI developer involvement is stated. The host technology consulting firm supplied the ChatGPT accounts through its own API-based interface, informed treated employees, and supplied past job performance records.
company_involvement.locator: PDF pp. 5-6 (printed pp. 4-5), Empirical Setting and Participants and Procedure

data_and_code.data_url: Not public; data and materials available upon request (confidentiality agreement with the firm), PDF p. 5 (printed p. 4)

eligibility.reason: Employees were individually randomized by random number generator to ChatGPT access or no access (PDF pp. 5-6). 250 employees were randomized and analyzed (Tables 1 and 3, N = 250). External raters scored novelty and usefulness of each employee's written response (criterion 3 met through S1-O2 and S1-O3); the supervisor rating rates the employee's weekly creative performance rather than a specific output.

one_line_finding: Among 250 consulting-firm employees, one week of ChatGPT access raised supervisor-rated creativity (4.14 vs 3.05, d = 1.25; multilevel gamma = 0.84, SE 0.10) and external-rater novelty (3.11 vs 2.78, d = 0.35; gamma = 0.25, SE 0.13) and usefulness (3.15 vs 2.87, d = 0.33; gamma = 0.17, SE 0.11, p = .136 with controls), Table 2 (PDF p. 8) and Table 3 (PDF p. 10).
open_questions: Was ChatGPT available to the treatment group while writing the August 15 privacy-protection response scored by external raters? The paper does not say; nothing indicates accounts were withdrawn, so it is coded as with AI.

Should the supervisor rating (creative performance over the week on the Zhou and George scale) count as an outcome scored on output? It is coded scored_on_output = false here, which makes the external-rater novelty the best output-scored primary candidate.
Per-arm counts are not printed; Table 1 reports the condition mean as 0.50 (N = 250).

Table 3 main estimates include controls measured on August 15, after assignment (creative self-efficacy, intrinsic motivation, job insecurity, task characteristics); the no-controls estimates sit in the supplement, which is not on file.
notes: PDF page = printed page + 1 because of the APA cover page. Multilevel models nest 250 employees in 30 supervisors in three departments, so standard errors are at the participant level with supervisor and department random intercepts. Footnote 2 says the no-controls multilevel models give p values from .006 to <.001 across the three creativity measures and cites Supplemental Materials S4, while the text cites Supplemental Table S5 Model 4 for the usefulness estimate without controls. Cognitive job resources (self-reported mediator, LLM effect gamma = 0.66, SE 0.10; Table 2: 3.38 vs 4.15, d = 0.92) and metacognitive strategies (self-reported moderator) are not listed as outcomes because they are self-reports. Moderated mediation results are on PDF p. 7. A lead in candidates.json says a 2026 preprint claims the study found lower later independent creativity; this PDF reports no after-AI outcome and mentions long-term dependence only as future research (PDF pp. 11-12, Limitations and Future Directions).
